title: SJL Engine scene (v0.1.0)
description: A complete level: settings, assets, prefabs and an entity tree. Run `sjl validate` for checks JSON Schema cannot express, such as entity references resolving and animation clips existing.

seed.description: Seeds the world RNG. Set it to make the run reproducible.

physics.description: World-level physics configuration. Created automatically from the scene's `settings.physics` block; you rarely add it by hand.

assets.description: Assets this scene needs. Referenced by id from component fields.

id.description: Unique id; what component fields reference

src.description: Path relative to the project root

width.description: Declared width; used in headless runs

id.description: Stable id, unique in the scene. Entity-reference fields point at it.

prefab.description: Name of a prefab to instance and override

Transform.description: Local position, rotation and scale. Every entity that exists in space needs one. Values are relative to the parent entity when there is one.

texture.description: Asset id from the scene `assets` list. Omit for an untextured colored quad. (texture id)

frame.description: Named region within an atlas texture. Empty means the whole texture.

size.description: Size in world units before Transform.scale is applied

anchor.description: Pivot within the sprite: [0,0] bottom-left, [0.5,0.5] center, [1,1] top-right

layer.description: Sort layer. Higher draws on top. Ties broken by `order`, then entity id.

Sprite.description: Draws a texture (or a solid color, if no texture is set) at the entity transform.

size.description: Width/height; for a circle, x is the diameter

points.description: Vertices for `line` and `polygon`, in local space

ShapeRenderer.description: Draws a primitive shape. Useful for prototypes, debug visuals and games that never load an image at all.

screenSpace.description: Ignore the camera and position in screen units — for HUDs

Text.description: Draws a string. Uses the backend's text support; no font asset required.

size.description: Half the visible height, in world units

bounds.description: Optional world-space clamp for the camera center

Camera.description: A view onto the world. Exactly one camera should be `active` at a time; the render system picks the active one with the highest priority.

target.description: Scene id of the entity to follow (entity id)

CameraFollow.description: Smoothly moves this entity toward a target entity. Put it on the camera.

tilesetTileSize.description: Size of one tile in the tileset image, in pixels

TilemapRenderer.description: Draws a grid of tiles from a tileset texture. `data` is row-major with row 0 at the BOTTOM, matching the +y-up axis convention. Tile index 0 means empty.

ParticleEmitter.description: A CPU particle emitter. Particles are simulated in the emitter's world space and drawn as colored quads. Deterministic: it draws from the world's seeded RNG.

Rigidbody.description:
Makes an entity move under the physics solver.
  dynamic   — moved by forces and collisions (a player, a crate)
  kinematic — moved by your code, pushes dynamics, is never pushed back (a moving platform)
  static    — never moves (the ground). Cheapest; static/static pairs are skipped entirely.

size.description: Full width and height in world units

offset.description: Local offset from the entity origin

isTrigger.description: Detect overlaps and fire trigger events, but never push anything

mask.description: Bitmask of layers to collide with; -1 = all

BoxCollider.description: An axis-aligned box collider. Rotation of the entity is ignored for collision — AABBs are what make the broadphase cheap and the solver stable. Use several boxes or a CircleCollider if you need rotated shapes.

CircleCollider.description: A circular collider. Cheapest shape, and the only one that rotates for free.

PhysicsSettings.description: World-level physics configuration. Created automatically from the scene's `settings.physics` block; you rarely add it by hand.

clips.description: Animation clips available on this entity

frames.description: Atlas frame names, in play order

events.description: Fires `animation:event` when playback reaches a frame

current.description: Name of the clip to play

SpriteAnimator.description: Plays frame-based sprite animations. Clips are declared inline so a scene file is self-contained; `sjl validate` checks that `current` names a clip that exists.

from.description: Start value. Omit to use the current value on start.

Tween.description: Animates one numeric or vec2 property over time. `target` is a dotted path into the entity's components, e.g. `Transform.position` or `Sprite.opacity`.

AudioSource.description: Plays a sound. In headless runs the audio backend records calls instead of making noise, so tests can assert that the jump sound fired without an audio device.

Lifetime.description: Destroys the entity after `seconds`. The standard way to clean up effects.

Health.description: Hit points. Nothing in the engine reads this — it exists because almost every game declares it identically, and having one shared shape means the editor and the debug overlay can display it.

speed.description: 0 means snap to the target instantly

halfLife.description: If > 0, smooth instead of moving at `speed`

Follow.description: Moves this entity toward another entity every frame. Simpler than a behavior.

rotation.description: Euler angles in DEGREES: x = pitch, y = yaw, z = roll (applied YXZ)

Transform3D.description: Local position, rotation and scale in 3D. Values are relative to the parent entity. Rotation is Euler degrees in YXZ (yaw, pitch, roll) order.

mesh.description: Primitive name (box, sphere, plane, quad, cylinder, cone) or a mesh asset id

color.description: Base color, multiplied with the texture

castShadow.description: Reserved; the forward renderer ignores it

layer.description: Sort layer; transparent meshes sort back-to-front

MeshRenderer.description: Draws a mesh. `mesh` names a built-in primitive (box, sphere, plane, cylinder, cone, quad) or an asset id. Materials are a deliberately small set: a color, an optional texture, and two lighting knobs.

fov.description: Vertical field of view, in degrees

orthoSize.description: Half the visible height, orthographic only

viewport.description: Normalized 0..1 screen rect, for split screen

Camera3D.description: A perspective (or orthographic) view onto the 3D world. The active camera with the highest priority wins. An unrotated camera looks down -z.

Light.description:
A light source.
  directional — infinitely far, shines along the entity's forward (-z). The sun.
  point       — radiates from the entity position, falling off over `range`.
  ambient     — uniform fill from every direction; position and rotation are ignored.

Skybox.description: A vertical gradient behind the scene. Cheap, and enough to make a 3D scene read as a space rather than a void — which a flat clear color does not.

target.description: Scene id of the entity to orbit (entity id)

sensitivity.description: Degrees per pixel of mouse movement

CameraOrbit.description: Orbits the camera around a target entity at a fixed distance. The standard third-person / inspection camera.

angularVelocity.description: Euler degrees per second. Visual only — collision shapes stay axis-aligned.

Rigidbody3D.description:
Makes an entity move under the 3D solver.
  dynamic   — moved by forces and collisions
  kinematic — moved by your code, pushes dynamics, is never pushed back
  static    — never moves; cheapest, and static/static pairs are skipped

Angular dynamics are deliberately not simulated: with AABB and sphere colliders there is no inertia tensor worth the name, and a tumbling box whose collider stays axis-aligned looks worse than one that does not tumble. Set `angularVelocity` to spin something visually; it will not affect collision.

offset.description: Local offset from the entity origin

mask.description: Bitmask of layers to collide with; -1 = all

BoxCollider3D.description: An axis-aligned box collider. Entity rotation is ignored for collision — AABBs are what keep the broadphase cheap and the solver stable. Compose several boxes, or use a SphereCollider, when you need a rotated shape.

SphereCollider.description: A spherical collider. Cheapest shape, and the only one that rotates for free.

slop.description: Overlap left unresolved, to stop jitter

Physics3DSettings.description: World-level 3D physics configuration. Created automatically from the scene's `settings.physics3d` block; you rarely add it by hand.

CharacterController3D.description: Marks a body as a walking character and holds its movement state. The FirstPersonController and ThirdPersonController behaviors read and write this, so both share one definition of "is this thing on the ground".

type.description: Eight-way movement driven by the moveX/moveY input actions. No gravity.
Side-scrolling movement with jumping, coyote time and jump buffering. Requires a Rigidbody and a collider; reads the moveX and jump actions.

coyoteTime.description: Grace period after leaving a ledge

jumpBuffer.description: Grace period for an early jump press

coyoteTime.description: Grace period after leaving a ledge

jumpBuffer.description: Grace period for an early jump press

type.description: Moves back and forth between two points, turning at each end.
Rotates the entity at a constant rate. Mostly for pickups and effects.
Moves the entity along a sine wave around its starting position.
Destroys an entity when something with a matching tag enters its trigger. The usual way to build coins, spikes and kill zones without writing code.

event.description: Optional world event to queue on trigger

velocity.description: Initial velocity, if the prefab has a Rigidbody

type.description: Rotates the entity to face the mouse cursor.
Raycasts downward and writes the result to Rigidbody.grounded. Use it when a character needs reliable ground detection on slopes or moving platforms, where contact normals alone can flicker.

distance.description: How far below the collider to probe
How far below the collider to probe

type.description: Follows a target entity with exponential smoothing. Frame-rate independent.

target.description: Scene id of the entity to follow (entity id)
Scene id of the entity to follow (entity id)

type.description: Mouse-look plus WASD movement on a capsule-ish body. Put it on the entity that carries the Camera3D, or on a body with the camera as a child.
Moves a character relative to the active camera and turns it to face travel. Pair with a CameraOrbit camera targeting the same entity.
Rotates the entity to face a target entity every frame.

target.description: Scene id of the entity to face (entity id)
Scene id of the entity to face (entity id)

type.description: Rotates the entity at a constant rate around each axis.
Bobs the entity up and down around its starting height.
Moves back and forth between two points along one axis.
Fires an event, or destroys the entity, once it falls below a height.

type.description: Destroys this entity when a tagged entity enters its trigger, optionally firing an event. The 3D counterpart of DestroyOnTrigger.
